source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Terminal Itô formula for sphere-valued integrated rows. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
For the initialized row process $X$ specified below, the generator is $\mathcal L_t f(X_t)$ with field value $u_t$ at the sample. There exists a real martingale $M$ for the given filtration with $M_0(\omega)=0$ at every sample, and the terminal increment has the displayed almost-sure decomposition.

The sample measure is finite. A standard Euclidean Brownian motion is given relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions. The finite coordinate set $I$ has decidable equality and the horizon $T$ is strictly positive.
Each initialized row is $x_i+\int_0^t b_i(s)\,ds+\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_{ij}(s)\,dB_j(s)$ using the library's completed stochastic integral on that horizon. The initial coordinates are strongly measurable in $\mathcal F_0$. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive with an integrable time section almost surely. Each noise entry is a strongly progressive product-space $L^2$ integrand.
On full-measure horizon events, the row process stays on the unit sphere at every $t\le T$ and the coefficients are $b(t)=-u_t-\lambda(t)(|I|-1)X_t$ and $\sigma_j(t)=\sqrt{2\lambda(t)}P_{X_t}e_j$ at all such times and all $j$. Here $P_we_j=e_j-w_jw$.
The real deterministic temperature is pointwise nonnegative up to $T$. The ambient test is $C^2$ at every sphere point, and a sphere point is supplied for the compact-range construction.
The ambient sphere Laplacian is $\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}}f(w)=\sum_j D^2f(w)[P_we_j,P_we_j]-(|I|-1)Df(w)[w]$.

f(X_T)-f(X_0)=\int_0^T[-Df(X_t)[u_t]+\lambda(t)\Delta_S^{\mathrm{ext}} f(X_t)]\,dt+M_T.

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I}
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
      filtration μ)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
  (η :
    I → I → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
  (x : Ω → I → ℝ) (hx : ∀ (i : I), MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable fun ω => x ω i) (b : I → NNReal → Ω → ℝ)
  (hb : ∀ (i : I), MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration (b i))
  (hbi :
    ∀ (i : I),
      ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun s => b i s ω)
          (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T))
  (fallback : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (hf : ∀ w ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f w)
  (u : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (temperature : NNReal → ℝ) (hNonneg : ∀ t ≤ T, 0 ≤ temperature t) :
  have A := fun i t ω =>
    x ω i +
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveDriftIntegral.prefixIntegralProcess (b i) t ω;
  have X := fun t ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 fun i =>
      A i t ω +
        ∑ j,
          AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ⋯
            hUsual t ω;
  (∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1) →
    (∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
        ∀ t ≤ T, (WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => b i t ω) = -u t ω - (temperature t * ↑(Fintype.card I - 1)) • X t ω) →
      (∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
          ∀ t ≤ T,
            ∀ (j : I),
              (WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => (η i j).process t ω) =
                √(2 * temperature t) •
                  local_symbol_235fd8b746d6 j (X t ω)) →
        ∃ M,
          MeasureTheory.Martingale M filtration μ ∧
            (∀ (ω : Ω), M 0 ω = 0) ∧
              ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ,
                f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) =
                  ∫ (s : NNReal),
                      -(fderiv ℝ f (X s ω)) (u s ω) +
                        temperature s *
                          local_symbol_e27025fd0d42 f
                            (X s ω) ∂AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T +
                    M T ω

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: Put d=card(I), c=real(max(d-1,0)) (natural-number subtraction before casting), E=R^I with Euclidean norm, S={x in E: ||x||=1}, V_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, and L_S f(x)=Laplacian(f)(x)-D^2 f(x)[x,x]-c*Df(x)[x]. Here Df is the Frechet derivative and D^2 f=D(Df). Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define A_i(t,omega)=x_i(omega)+integral_0^t b_i(s,omega)ds and X(t,omega)=(A_i(t,omega)+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t,omega))_i. The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).

Domains: Omega measurable, I finite with decidable equality, mu a finite measure, filtration on R_+, T>0, B:R_+ x Omega->E. eta:I x I->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); x:Omega->R^I; b:I x R_+ x Omega->R; fallback in S; f:E->R; u:R_+ x Omega->E; a:R_+->R.

Quantifiers: Universally the spaces, instances, filtration,mu,T,B, hB,hT,hUsual,eta,x,hx,b,hb,hbi,fallback,f,hf,u,a,hNonneg. Then three implications, respectively sphere membership, drift identity, diffusion-column identities. After all three premises there exists a real process M on R_+ x Omega.

Assumptions: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). Each x_i is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(0), b_i strongly progressive, and b_i(.,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for mu-a.e. omega. f is C^2 at every sphere point, a(t)>=0 for every t<=T, and fallback is an actual sphere point. Assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T, X(t,omega) belongs to S; assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T, b(t,omega)=-u(t,omega)-a(t)*c*X(t,omega); assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T and j, eta_.j(t,omega)=sqrt(2*a(t))*V_j(X(t,omega)). No explicit continuity or measurability assumption on u or a is listed beyond these statements.

Conclusion: There exists a filtration-martingale M with respect to mu, M(0,omega)=0 for every omega, and for mu-a.e. omega: f(X(T,omega))-f(X(0,omega))=integral_0^T [-Df(X(s,omega))[u(s,omega)]+a(s)*L_S f(X(s,omega))]ds+M(T,omega).

Scopes: The martingale assertion is for the whole R_+-indexed M, while the displayed decomposition is asserted only at terminal time T. Zero initial value is pointwise for all omega. Three premises hold a.e. uniformly over the fixed horizon. The measure is finite, not separately required to be a probability measure.

Constant dependencies: The existential M may depend on all preceding data, proofs and fallback; no M is specified uniquely. fallback enforces nonemptiness of the sphere and is not present in the displayed terminal identity. No deterministic bound constant is asserted.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoCompactEuclideanFormula
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereDiffusionGenerator
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoGeneratorIntegrability

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SphereItoIntegratedRows

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 EuclideanBrownianCoordinates ItoIntegralProcess
  ProgressiveDriftIntegral ItoInitializedDrift ItoEuclideanRowRegularity ItoCompactEuclideanFormula ItoGeneratorIntegrability
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereProjectedNoise
  AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereDiffusionGenerator

/-- Apply the compact Euclidean Itô formula to an actual process on the unit
sphere and identify its generator from the projected columns and radial drift.
The drift and Hessian terms are integrable by the row conditions. -/
theorem ito_formula_sphere_of_integrated_rows
    {Ω I : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : ℝ≥0}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration μ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
    (η : I → I → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
    (x : Ω → I → ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, StronglyMeasurable[filtration 0] (fun ω => x ω i))
    (b : I → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (hb : ∀ i, IsStronglyProgressive filtration (b i))
    (hbi : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Integrable (fun s => b i s ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T))
    (fallback : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1)
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ w ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f w)
    (u : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I)
    (temperature : ℝ≥0 → ℝ)
    (hNonneg : ∀ t ≤ T, 0 ≤ temperature t) :
    let A := fun (i : I) (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) => x ω i + prefixIntegralProcess (b i) t ω
    let X := fun (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => A i t ω + ∑ j : I,
      itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω)
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1) →
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i t ω) =
      -u t ω - (temperature t * ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) • X t ω) →
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ j : I, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (η i j).process t ω) =
      Real.sqrt (2 * temperature t) • projectedNoiseColumn j (X t ω)) →
    ∃ M : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ, Martingale M filtration μ ∧ (∀ ω, M 0 ω = 0) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) =
        (∫ s, -fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (u s ω) + temperature s * sphereLaplacian f (X s ω)
          ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) + M T ω) := by
  intro A X hSphere hDrift hColumns
  have hK := isCompact_sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1
  obtain ⟨θ, _, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ :=
    ito_formula_compact_euclidean_at_horizon hB hT hUsual η x hx b hb hbi hK fallback f hf hSphere
  let M (s : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) := ∑ q : I × I,
    itoIntegralProcess (θ q) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian q.2) hUsual s ω
  refine ⟨M, hM, hM0, ?_⟩
  have hA (i : I) := initialized_drift_progressive_continuous_boundedVariation
    (fun ω => x ω i) (hx i) (b i) (hb i) (hbi i)
  have hAmeas (i : I) (s : ℝ≥0) (_ : s ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A i s) μ :=
    (((hA i).1.stronglyAdapted s).mono (filtration.le s)).aestronglyMeasurable
  obtain ⟨_, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas
    (fun i => (hA i).2.2.mono fun _ h => h.1)
  have hInt := ae_integrable_euclidean_generator_terms η b hbi X hXc hSphere f hf
  filter_upwards [hIto, hSphere, hDrift, hColumns, hInt] with ω hω hS hbω hηω hint
  let ν := TimeMeasure.upTo T
  let v (s : ℝ≥0) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i s ω)
  let σ (j : I) (s : ℝ≥0) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (η i j).process s ω)
  let D (s : ℝ≥0) := fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (v s)
  let Q (s : ℝ≥0) := (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ j : I,
    fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (X s ω) (σ j s) (σ j s)
  have hD : Integrable D ν := hint.1
  have hQ : Integrable Q ν := hint.2
  change f (X T ω) - f (X 0 ω) =
    (∫ s, D s ∂ν) + (∫ s, Q s ∂ν) + M T ω at hω
  rw [hω, ← integral_add hD hQ]
  apply congrArg (· + M T ω)
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards [TimeMeasure.ae_le_terminal T] with s hs
  have hUnit : ‖X s ω‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 (hS s hs)
  simp only [D, Q, v, σ, hbω s hs, hηω s hs]
  exact ito_generator_eq_sphereLaplacian f hUnit (u s ω) (hNonneg s hs)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SphereItoIntegratedRows

steps.text: The row integrability theorem makes both terms integrable on the same almost-sure horizon event. The projected column identity combines their integrands.
